result.topic_en: Gauss defines partial and general 'mensurae' of a polynomial in roots of unity (norm-type products f(ε)f(ε^{n-1})), proves they are positive sums of squares, derives inequalities with the norm D, and computes a degree-5 norm form with numerical checks.
result.transcription:
Math 16 \quad (7) [-44 f-] 7
Es sei
$m = a + a'\varepsilon + a''\varepsilon\varepsilon + a'''\varepsilon^3 + etc. = f\varepsilon$
$\mathfrak{D} = f\varepsilon . f\varepsilon\varepsilon . f\varepsilon^3 \ldots f\varepsilon^{n-1}$
$M = f\varepsilon . f\varepsilon^{n-1} = - b'(\varepsilon+\varepsilon^{n-1}) - b''(\varepsilon^2+\varepsilon^{-2}) - b'''(\varepsilon^3+\varepsilon^{-3}) \ldots$
So ist
$2b' = (a-a')^2 + (a'-a'')^2 + (a''-a''')^2 + etc.$
$2b'' = (a-a'')^2 + (a'-a''')^2 + (a''-a^{IV})^2 + etc.$
etc.
Hier sind also $b', b'', b'''$ lauter positive Grössen; sie heissen Partialmensuren von $m$; so wie ihre Summe
$b' + b'' + b''' + etc. = n(aa + a'a' + a''a'' \ldots) - (a + a' + a'' + etc.)^2$
die Generalmensur.
Setzt man
$f\varepsilon . f\varepsilon^{n-1} = c'$
$f\varepsilon\varepsilon . f\varepsilon^{n-2} = c''$ etc.
So ist $c' + c'' + c''' + etc. + c^{\frac12(n-1)} = b' + b'' + b''' + etc. + b^{\frac12(n-1)}$
$c'(\varepsilon+\varepsilon^{n-1}) + c''(\varepsilon\varepsilon+\varepsilon^{n-2}) + c'''(\varepsilon^3+\varepsilon^{n-3}) + etc. = 2(b'+b''+b'''+etc. + b^{\frac12(n-1)}) - nb'$
$c'(2-\varepsilon-\varepsilon^{n-1}) + c''(2-\varepsilon\varepsilon-\varepsilon^{n-2}) + c'''(2-\varepsilon^3-\varepsilon^{n-3}) + etc. = nb'$
$b' > \frac{n-1}{2n}(n\mathfrak{D})^{\frac{2}{n-1}}$
$b'+b''+b'''+etc. > \frac{(n-1)}{2}\mathfrak{D}^{\frac{2}{n-1}}$

methods.what: Definition of the norm D of f(ε) as product over all conjugates
Product f(ε)f(ε^{-1}) expanded with coefficients b', b'', ...
Partial mensurae expressed as sums of squares of cyclic coefficient differences (hence positive)
General mensura as sum of partial mensurae, equal to n·Σa² − (Σa)²
methods.quote: $b' + b'' + b''' + etc. = n(aa + a'a' + a''a'' \ldots) - (a + a' + a'' + etc.)^2$

methods.what: Linear relation between conjugate products c and partial mensurae b
Lower bounds of partial and general mensura in terms of the norm D
Explicit norm form for n=5 (product of conjugates of a+bx+cx²+dx³+ex⁴)
Numerical check of the specialized norm form with a=1,b=2,c=4
Linear relations among conjugates A,B,C,D used to isolate a coefficient
Trigonometric form of conjugate pair and difference identity
